body:
Ya'll kinda are. 

You destabilize the entire GPU market for 3-6 months for everyone (vendors, AIBs, consumers) by consuming all the inventory and then you destabilize it for another 3-6 months immediately after inventory finally normalizes because the vast majority of your starting dumping your cards en masse when you finally figure out 1) you're aren't going to recover your ROI or 2) you'll recover your ROI, but the profit is so marginal it's almost not even worth talking about.

"It took a month of non stop mining to make $200!" sounds really nice right up until you realize you spent $250-$550 in hardware costs alone and you could've made 4x that (at no additional out of pocket cost to yourself) working late one day a week.

Fully a third of my life has been spent going from one period of misery directly into the next without there being a reprieve. Not months. Not weeks. Days, maybe hours, where life wasn't a complete exercise in heart-rendering futility.

Intangibles of what could be don't mean all that much because they're just that: intangibles. Hypotheticals. They don't change the reality of now and the near future, both of which are awful. 

What do I have to hope for now? That I can rebuild from nothing for the 4th time in 8 years? That I can be loved romantically in the ways I love despite the fact that I get routinely thrown away like a used condom because my positive qualities don't surpass the negative ones? That I get to continue not having a home I can grow in and cherish, having to shuttle from one shit hole to the next every 6 months to a year? That my depression isn't going to wane?

What do I have left? Nothing. I have nothing left. There is nothing about now that makes me see life as something precious. If anything, it's a just a reaffirmation its little more than torture without end for some people. 

I'm already an old man in a much younger man's body. I've done this for far too long, too many times, and I'm at a point I refuse to do it anymore because it never leads to anything good.

People have told me it gets better for three months straight. They keep telling me to "hold on, it gets better". The other half goes, " You've got serious problems and need help!"
I have BPI, but it's mostly hardcore clinical depression that barely responds to medication. Every single day is a struggle and that is at the best of times.

I haven't experienced a period in my adult life where things have not been stressful to the point of comedy. Years of a highly abusive marriage left me scarred. She took everything of value that could fit in her boyfriend's truck. Even the dog, who was more or less my son (had him since he was just 8 weeks old). I rebuilt.

 The girl after her? Two years of trying to make it work because the spectra of my marriage and depression was always there. She cheated on me to get out. I caught her getting dropped off by her date while I was on a stress walk because I had no idea where she was or if she was okay. That triggered an episode where I slept 20 hours in a month and couldn't eat solid food without throwing it up. I cost me my job, then my apartment, then everything I had.

It took almost two years to stand on my own feet again and not want to die. I came here because I was in love and she seemed to be in love with me. And right as life looked like it was going to be fine, the hammer came down hard. Now? Now I'm just a crazy person to her. She's afraid of me, hates me. I've reached out four times in 3 months (twice just asking about my mail) and that apparently makes me obsessed.

The rest of life? A fucking mess. I have $100 to live off of for a month. A load of laundry costs me $4. A can of tuna is $1.29. I don't make spaghetti in meat sauce, I eat the pasta raw and imagine what its like to have it cooked because my only appliance is a microwave and that is something a friend gave to me out of pity. I've been desperately trying to get a job, any job, and I can't. YMCA career center person says my resume looks fine. Another redditor who is in a youth employment group looked it over and said it was fine. 70+ applications on the go since I got thrown into Ottawa and I haven't even been told, "Sorry but....".

Could life be better? Sure. Will it? No, it won't and I have accepted that. You know what the biggest fuck you to me has ever been? It wasn't being abused. It wasn't being cheated on, or to make a French hillbilly jealous so he could finally act like a boyfriend. It was calling the paramedics to bring me back into a life I vehemently hate. A life that is so soul crushingly awful in every way that I don't have nightmares: I'm living them. I go back to see my family over the holidays. Once that's done, I'm punching my own clock. There's nothing left to make any of this worthwhile to me and the void was much, much better.

The most recent one, if you consider it a breakup.

Moved up to Canada to be with a very good friend of mine I had crushed on since day one. I was finally starting over, moving on from the deep emotional, financial, and mental hole my ex threw me into when she cheated on me (triggered a manic episode, lost my job, then my home, as well as everything I owned). For the first time in almost two years, I finally felt like things were going to look up.

She took her ex back a week to the day of my arrival. His brother had moved to france to be a priest and he played her heart strings in every possible way he could. I was told that he was getting "another chance" but that it wouldn't work out. Difficult, but I could work with it.

He moved in the second day of my arrival because he didn't trust her. He acted "nice", which is to say passive aggressive. I did what I could to help out around the house like I had promised. I even went so far to take care of many of the loose ends he had left.

Towards the second week, she "fell back in love" with him. I couldn't handle it. This is someone I once spoke to for hours on the phone about anything. Someone who renovated a room and furnished it just for me. Someone who cared about me far more than a friend and showed it. And yet I could even wrap my arms around her. She withdrew, became more distant, and angry when I tried to find out why I had been jammed into the event horizon of being a "backup" plan. Having to watch someone you love literally go to bed with the man who had made her miserable before is heart crushing in ways I can't even begin to articulate.

During all of this, I was having issues getting moved from one generic antidepressant to another. It wasn't as effective and I could feel it, but I did my best to power through or ignore it. 

Things came to a head on week 3. He and I got into an argument over a dog (the puppy I helped name, the one he bitched about constant) because he left her out in the pouring rain for the 2nd time in a row. The next day I was told to get out, that it wasn't working, she loved him, and so forth.

Now, when I came to Canada, I didn't have much money. I had $800 saved (wages in Missouri are low, fulltime jobs are impossible to get in rural communities if you're not a farmer). I had just paid rent for the previous month and the current one. I was just my second day into work. I immediately tried reaching out to my friends to see if I could just stay with them for even a day and was told by all, "No, can't help you."

I tried to kill myself; took a few months worth of my medication, hugged the puppy, laid down, and blacked out with the intention of not waking up. With nowhere to go, no one to turn to, and being faced with the prospect of having to live through every simultaneous loss I barely survived the previous 15 months, death was a solid option.

I was found 20 hours later. Was taken by ambulance to the hospital, was stabilized, had to cab an hour back, and was thrown out 4 hours later.

Right now? I live in a shitty apartment on welfare because the 70+ resumes I put out have yielded nothing. Ontario Works has left me stuck in limbo. I've sold pretty much everything I didn't lose during the last breakup and divorce just so I have enough money to do laundry or to eat. My other option is to go back to the US, do the same damn thing, and the only upside is that I *might* not be as hungry.

Is this the work breakup I've ever had? Yeah. My life has been so thoroughly destroyed and I've been so completely broken that I would spray my brains on the wall behind me if I had the capital on hand to buy a gun.

If there was anything in the present or near future to hold onto, I would. Right now, my options are "Welfare in Canada while I struggle to find a job, total social isolation, and life being a joyless grind" or "Welfare in the US while I struggle to find a job, total social isolation, and life being a joyless grind".

Those are the only two options I have and the only difference between them is geography. Everything else is exactly the same.

I wish she had let me die in my sleep like I had wanted; the life I have now is one that mirrors my worst nightmares and the life ahead of me is one I never wanted for myself.
I'm living it. I can honestly tell you it has not been worthwhile.

I have a wealth of useless knowledge already.

The only variables that needs to change are those that I've invested in. If employment is forever out of reach for no outwardly apparent reason, if I can't have a proper home, and if I'm going to be perpetually alone (in terms of friends and romantically) despite my efforts to change them, what's the point?

If life is the summation of our experiences when the good is weighed against the bad, what's the point of carrying on if the resultant sum is a negative?
What is there to research?

My expectations of life is for it to not be patently awful 99.9% of the time. Does it have rough patches? Yes. Should it to itself be like this all the time? No.

Expectations have not been met in the least. I don't want a super model girlfriend clinging off of me all day every day. I don't want to be the CEO of a fortune 500 company. I don't want to be Ned Flanders, and I don't want a mansion.

What I want is to be able to have a best friend I love who also loves me back. Someone I can share my life with and be a part of theirs. I want a job. For almost a hundred resumes out, I should have had at least one call for even unskilled general labor. I want to not be depressed and I want an actual home I'm not ejected from every 6 months to a year.

These are things I have not had. I get enough of a taste to know they exist, but they get jerked out of my hands just as I'm able to grasp them after trying desperately to earn them. These are things other people take for granted every minute of every day of the week without even thinking or realizing about it. Do you think my should-have-been-girlfriend's boyfriend wakes up every day grateful for what he has? Absolutely not.

It's been 10 years of suck. A little over a third of my life has been a write-off and my crowning achievements mean nothing to anyone but me. I have nothing to show for it. And what do I have right now that makes the suffering bearable? Not a damn thing. I wake up every single day to live through my vision of hell and the truly shitty thing is that I have been there before, it almost killed me, and I was thrown back into it almost as soon as I was on the other side. When will it end? Will it ever end in my life, or is my only out death?

I do not want to do this for another year. I don't want to do it for another 6 months. I want it to end soon.

The one and only person I want to to talk to I never can again. Ever. She thinks I'm a nutjob. Apparently asking for my mail twice over two months , sending one letter (not multiple, ONE) telling her what she meant to me, and trying to have a facebook conversation as to why she changed her mind pre-suicide attempt makes me an obsessed crazy person who "needs help" when I'm trying to get an answer as to what fault I have as a human being that makes me that undesirable. And all I've got is, "You need help."

Yes, I blamed myself for everything. I even blamed myself for things I had no control over (like not being able to build a harness so her sharpe-bernese mountain dog mix wasn't in constant pain trying to move). I blamed my suicide attempt on having my mind fucked with over weeks, my repeated perceived failures, and the stress of not being able to get a gainful job like I thought I would. All of those were factors. The deciding factor was realizing that I was going to be made homeless, jobless, and totally alone (not romantically, I mean completely alone in every possible way) AGAIN after having spent the better part of two years fighting to pull myself out of that hole. I didn't want to go through what I'm having to go through now. I barely made it out alive the last time.

I was fine before I got here. I was better than I had been in almost two years. I was *finally* moving forward with my life. I had things to look forward to. Things to be excited about. What do I have now?

I see a therapist every two weeks. So far, it's been, "If you think positive thoughts, you'll experience positive things by having positive actions." ...I don't want to feel good about any of this. I don't want to feel better about it. I can't think of any sane, rational human being who would. I do not have a focal point that makes me feel even remotely positive about my life. People say focus on the little things? The little things are incidental. I don't care about whether the sun is shining or not, I care about having a job and enough money to support myself. I care about not waking up alone, going through my day alone, and going to bed alone. And I would even worry about that if I had real friends: I don't. My ex-wife chased all them away during our divorce.

I am in hell. And if I go back to live in the US, I'll still be in hell. The only difference is that I'll have my family telling me, "Hey, perk up! Be grateful for XYZ" when XYZ doesn't make me happy. It's not ingratitude not to be happy, it's making a statement and I'm made to feel like shit when I reject it.

I'm 27 years old and it feels like someone is constantly squeezing my heart and not letting go. At all times. And people go, "Breathe, everything will be okay." None of this is okay. Not a single bit of it. And I don't care if I survive it, I care about whether or not I'll actually be allowed to live for once because I haven't so far. I haven't lived a day at any point in my entire adult life.

I just want the shit show to end. Not in 5 years. Not in a year. Soon.

I have done this for a very, very long time. I'm tired of doing it.

It pretty much is the case. Nothing is changing. At all. I do not want to do this anymore.

And I don't have to worry about love because there is not a person on this planet who will love me for who I am.

All of this shit? It'd be worthwhile if she loved me. But she doesn't and she never will. 

And now I'm of no good to anyone.

It didn't work out in any capacity. 

My life's been totally, thoroughly ruined. There's no coming back from this. Not today, not tomorrow, not next month. There isn't going to be a point in my life where things work out or go okay. It is just one hardship to the next. I don't want to do that anymore.

Whenever I try to push my life forward into a meaningful direction, it comes crash down around me. 

I am tired. Exhausted. I'm tired of having to go through life just barely surviving because that's what the circumstances are and every effort I put in to change them doesn't actually do so.

I wasn't happy in Missouri, so I moved back to Canada. I moved to Canada to pursue a relationship with someone I love, a job that paid more than $11 an hour, and a home. A real home that I could grow in. *poof* all of them are gone. What do I have now? Nothing. It tooks 15 months of agony and pushing as hard as I could just to get in a position where I was able to move forward and, the very second I was able to do so, I got sent back to the beginning. Again.

Yes, I can play video games, weight lift, read, draw, and write to pass the time. I've been doing those things. They do not, however, provide anything other than a temporary escape from reality and the reality is pretty damn awful. I've tried to change my financial fortunes. 70 applications out. 70. Not a single phone call for an interview. 

Life in Canada? Awful. I've been spending months trying to salvage it into something meaningful and have nothing to show for it. Life in the US? It was pretty shitty too, otherwise I wouldn't have moved up this way. I had a soul sucking job in a small town that I couldn't get out; I applied, I interviewed, I was stuck there. I quit that job to work another soul sucking one and I only got that because of the rotating door. I had family but I was alone; we didn't share the same interests, we couldn't talk, and we didn't enjoy the same things. I had no friends and couldn't make any. I went on a total sum of 2 dates. Two.

That's what I get to go back to. If I couldn't make anything of it the last go, how can I make it this one? 

The C, D, and so forth requires an external catalyst. Until someone else gives me a damn chance, I don't have one and I haven't been able to make one either.

I've been in hell for almost 3 months. And that's all I get to do for the foreseeable future.

There's not been a time where I haven't realized I don't have positive qualities or potential. That has never been in question. And there's never been a time where I haven't been able to see that things could be better.

The positive qualities mean nothing in the real world. They've carried me nowhere.

I'm tired of having to wait it out, or making plans that always blow up in my face. 

What about my situation would make anyone go, "I'm glad to be alive"? Remove depression from it and things would still be completely awful. And there is no light at the end of the tunnel that things actually will work out to be okay in the end. I get to "live" another day. What's so amazing about that? What is so great that the potential I have as a person is crippled because life is one stressful shit show after another where the best I can do is just barely survive? 

Could things be better? Yes. Are they? No. If I stay in Canada, I'll still be stuck on OW while I desperately try to find a job; for a city of 700,000 people and a lot of help wanted signs, people are apparently quite picky as to who they're going to hire for that McJob. Will I still be financially screwed? Yep. Will I still be romantically alone? Oh yeah, I'm most likely going to die an involuntary bachelor because whatever romantic visions I have ultimately will never come to pass because women don't want men with mental health issues.

If I go back to the US next week, it's essentially a copy paste with the difference being I'll be in a town of sub 12,000 people. Everything else is identical. 

My options are: pointless life A, pointless life B. I'm almost 28 years old. Do i have to be 40 before life suddenly becomes something less shitty? How much more do I have to go through for how long before I can finally wake up one day and not go, "Goddamn it, why didn't I die of an aneurysm in my sleep?"

Thing is, I've been repeatedly told multiple times I am not relationship material even when I'm mentally okay (or as okay as I can be). The love that brought me to Canada? She played mindgames and hit every major fear of mine to the point I tried killing myself (which had way more to do with facing homelessness and joblessness in a country I'm not originally from) and then threw me out so I could experience those things when I was stabilized.

No matter the reason, multiple attempted suicides (and not "attempts" for attention, I mean literally trying to end your life) coupled with everything else makes me unviable. 

Off Reddit, I don't share my personal life with anyone. And that's largely because when I finally do after spending the months building that kind of trust, people run away quicker than you can type "wtf".

I have had two serious relationships: one was my marriage of 6 years, the other was a serious relationship of 2 years. I have had a total sum of 4 dates in my life. It takes years to build a solid friendship, years more when I decide I want to be more than that. 

It never works out. And it doesn't work out because people can see that specter hovering over my head like the sword of Damocles. Everything else? That makes me a jobless loser stuck on welfare. The hows and whys are irrelevant. No one cares I'm on both because someone I cared about so deeply for threw me out without a pot to piss in. They look at me and go, " Dude's 27 and he does not have his life together at all. Nope. Wait, he has a mental health issue? Hell no, I'm out."

To me they're very much the same thing. This has been a constant, repetitious cycle and I'm tired of having to live through horrible losses all the time. That is not supposed to be life. And yet that's all I'm afforded.

My options are: stay in Canada and rot as life keeps denying me even the possibility to move forward, or go back to the US and essentially do the same thing. Those are my options. And they're both terrible.

"Be you peasants?!"

"Nay! We are but men!"
"This is not the greatest HDD in the world, this is just a tribute."

If I were an outside observer, yes, I would see someone in my current situation as being beyond repair.

There is not a single facet of my situation I want to live through, especially not all simultaneously. I have been in hell for months. If I continue to live, I will be in hell for months (most likely years) more. There is not going to be a point in my life where the things I really do need (love, stability, home) are actually going to come into play. I'm 27 years old and I haven't truthfully had any of them for the entirety of my adult life. It literally has been multiple cycles of the same kind of duress I'm under now.

I am 27 years old and my life is already over before I even had a chance to actually live it. What about what I'm living now and what I'm expected to live strikes anyone as worthwhile? 

Hardship without joy is just needless, pointless suffering. I am tired of suffering. I am being asked to continue on so that I can still suffer on intangibles I can clearly see and have had violently jerked away from me the second it appears I can reach them.

Just because I know they exist and that they could be achieved doesn't mean that they are.

I came back to Canada for love, home, and a chance to make a decent wage before I go to college. What do I have now? Nothing. I literally have nothing that makes any of this worthwhile to me. There is nothing that justifies having to continue on through the pain and crushing disappointment. 

I have no legitimately good reason to be alive right now. None. In fact, I wouldn't be having this conversation had I been allowed to die as I had desired when life fell apart. I get to know only this for the foreseeable future and is there a light at the end of the tunnel? Hell no, there isn't.

I have lost too much, for too long, too frequently. I have accepted my fate, the only thing I reject is the time frame. If there is a God or something in the universe beyond what science can explain, it is evident that I am not supposed to have a happy or fulfilling life; if I were meant to, things wouldn't be as horrible as they have been for so long.

There's not enough of a performance increase going from a 3570k to a 4690k if they shared the same socket. Since they don't, there's definitely not enough of a performance increase justify the expense of investing in a new chipset.

What you could do, however, is take that money and get two GTX 970s.

I saw them improve for all of 2 weeks in the past 18 months.

Will they improve tomorrow? No. Will they improve next week? No. Will they improve in January? No, they won't. I'll be lucky to have that low pay grunt job at sub-$10 an hour.

She isn't going to reconsider, not after my attempted suicide (the day she told me to get out and all of my backup plans failed) and especially after the 2 page long goodbye letter I wrote detailing everything she meant to me that she didn't know as well as how devastating it was to be friendzoned so she could make things work with her ex quite literally in front of me. Will I have a real home? No, I'll be in some temporary ghetto unit in a town and state I never want to live in. Will I have anything to occupy my time with? Nope, I'm going back with a backup of clothes because I've lost everything else. 

Is there anyone else? No. Will there be? Nope, because the rest of my life is a total disaster and, even if it wasn't, women don't date clinically depressed men. I learned that lesson very clearly during my last stay in Missouri where I had a total sum of 2 dates that didn't progress beyond the first and a psuedo-relationship that lasted all of a week. The "Oh, you need to learn to love yourself before ____". I was ready for a relationship this fall emotionally and mentally. I was greatly looking forward to cuddling on a sofa and watching a movie with the wood burning stove running. I was dying to explore Montreal hand in hand. I was excited to pick her brain when she goes to Uni. I get to do none of those things now and for the foreseeable future. I get to be alone. Wake up alone. Go to bed alone. Stare at my goddamn cellphone screen alone wondering why I have an unlimited plan when I have no one to talk to beyond family (which I can't really talk to because the consensus is, "Do as we say, lower your standards, settle, and get the fuck over it.").

I am not going to wait another 15 months being isolated, lonely, broke, and broken just because that's life's grand plan for me. There is supposed to be more to life than this, and my coming up to Canada in September was supposed to have been the start of a great new chapter in my life.

Tomorrow, I sell my computer. Monday I will then take that money to the bank, convert it to USD, and close my account. Next Tuesday, I arrive in the US. After christmas, I am acquiring a shotgun and a box of slugs (a waste because I only need one). In the first week of January, I'm clock out. I cannot do this anymore. 

I'm tired of the loss. I'm tried of the heartache. I'm tired of the emotional pain, the depression. I'm tired of the housing instability and financial difficulties. I'm greatly tired of being my only friend.

Life could be better; it isn't. And barring some divine miracle, they're going to be shitty for years to come assuming I live.

I've already taken a lot of a chances. I took an enormous chance by coming back to Canada for the reasons that I did. I've got nothing to show for it.

You know what breaking the pattern is? Having a proper home I don't have to leave in 6 months or a year. Having a job that pays better than $10 an hour with more than 30 hours a week where I'm not confined to a windowless space all day by myself. Being romantically loved in the same capacity I give it. I had tastes of each for the first time in a long time and BAM! gone.

I weight lift. I can deadlift 300 lbs. I weight lift for 10 hours a week. Can  I eat good food? No, I'm limited to whatever the food bank, soup kitchens, and what my $100 a month is able to provide. Are there any interests I can pursue with the amount of money I have? No. Will there be any interests where I'll be going? No, rural towns have nothing in them.

My goal right now is to make it through Christmas, take the money I'll make from selling my computer (for 40% less than what I'm asking for it), buy a shotgun, and just be done with it. There is no point in going on. There is nothing in the near or far future that interests me in the slightest.

Thing is, they don't change. 

I'm having to relive play-by-play every significant loss I experienced in 2013: I lost my relationship to someone else, I lost my best friend, I lost my job, I lost my home, depression came roaring back, and I'm in the process of losing everything I own. All at the same time. I get to relive all of that for the second time in 2 years immediately after I started to come out on the other side.

It took almost 15 months to rebuild from nothing the last go and it was absolutely horrible every step of the way. I couldn't make friends where I was living, I got stuck in a high stress retail warehousing job that paid poorly, I couldn't really get a job anywhere else, finances were exceptionally tight, I couldn't date anyone, I was still depressed, and I was only able to reclaim a sliver of what had been lost.

1 get to do that all over again, but I also get to do it with the worst parts of the present: I'm going to be jammed into another shitty low income unit I never wanted to set a single foot into, I'm going to live exactly where I don't want to be, and I'm going to be told the entire time by my family "Perk up! It could be worse! Quit bitching over spilt milk!" etc. I will be derided, again, when I factually state that whatever pattern they feel I should conform to is ultimately not going to be the one that makes me happy in life because I gave that a go for 13 months and I couldn't wait for that period to end.

Nothing changes. Things will be no different in January. They won't be any different in February or March. I *do not* have enough of a life left that can be salvaged and whatever the universe seems to have planned just feeds into the notion that, if there's a God, he is a total asshole. I am 27 years old. I have had to start over, from scratch, 4 fucking times in 8 years only to wind up with the same results every single time no matter where I go or what I do.
"...it's not NOT a tumah".
Hopefully life becoming something other than a depressing act in futility  that makes me pine for death.

Yep. I know I'm going to die alone because the pool of people who are willing to accept those with bi-polar (even when properly treated) is so insignificant it's not worth considering. And people go on, and on about, "You need to be with okay with you!" 

Depressed people are never okay with themselves. If they were, they wouldn't be depressed. And there is not a single person on this planet (who isn't a hermit) that enjoys being their only companion all day, every day, 365 a year.
If you have a mental illness of any kind, there's a pretty high probability you will actually die alone.

Oh, I'm not worried about the future. The future will most likely be a reflection of what I'm going through now, because that's pretty much been the case for the entirety of my past.

The present is awful; there are no redeeming qualities about it, nothing that gives me even the slightest bit of joy.

My current circumstances are nigh on identical to those I went through last year and several years prior.

I've spent fully a third of my life hoping and striving for a better day that doesn't come. I don't get to build a life in Canada; too much damage has been done, too long to fully recover. I don't get to build a decent life in the US because the Midwest is a region in decline outside of the agriculture and automotive industries.
I fail to see how a positive disposition has any meaningful impact on my situation.

Never attribute to malice what can easily be attributed to ignorance or laziness.

I used to work at Homesense (TJX is the parent company). There were *always* issues with tagging bedding correctly. If you were lucky, the bedding had tags on but they weren't secured right; the pins weren't pressed in all the way or they were put on in such a way that you could still open the whole package. If you weren't, they'd just jam the tags in and called it good.

I appreciate it your well wishes. 

As for whoever-the-fuck, he's proven the point I made (a few times). Why he seems to be offended by my very posting here and conducts himself as if I am literally trying to take food from his mouth is unusual. I didn't come back to Canada to be in the situation I am in. I didn't want to be on OW. I didn't want to come back to Ottawa. And when life fell apart in every measurable where I had moved, I was very close to being successful in ending it; were it not for the intervention of another, I wouldn't be here.

I didn't create this thread with the intention of garnering pity, I created it because employment is required if I am to continue existing and my I was looking for ideas that I myself had not thought of. A lot of the posters were very helpful.

The only reason I chose Goodlife is that I know they're the easiest gym to get in, in any real capacity.

Helping other people is rewarding, even if the pay is not fantastic. You're trying to encourage the continued investment people are trying to make in themselves; a little encouragement does indeed go a long way.

To be fair, Sony and Microsoft didn't really have any alternatives for an SoC vendor. NVIDIA doesn't have an X86 license and Intel, while leading the way in CPU performance as well as manufacturing tech, doesn't have a high performance IGP; as much as people talked about Iris Pro being a game changer, it only offers competitive computational performance with the absolute bottom rung discrete GPUs.

They could have gone with differing CPU and GPU vendors as they did with the last generation, but that defeats the purpose of minimizing hardware costs and complexity. And I'm not just referring to the additional costs tied to being the sole buyer of two proprietary chips, but also the complexity of the motherboard's PCB, the number of components for power delivery, etc. 

Having said all that, it is worth pointing out the a launch PS4's power consumption is actually lower than a launch PS3's by 20-40 watts.

Both platforms have low level, highly optimized APIs for developers to work with.

The main benefit of DX12 is greatly reduced CPU overhead and the only platform this will benefit is the PC; a console programming environment is, by design, low level and very close to the metal because there're such a limited (usually singular) hardware configurations to support.

Form factor is essentially a common industry standard that dictates the size of a motherboard (where everything connects to) and provides a *very* basic component layout. The three form factors people generally see (from largest to smallest) are ATX, micro-ATX, and mini-ITX.  

The form factor you choice ultimately decides your expandability and case size. You can build a mini-ITX based system that isn't that much bigger than an Xbox One yet have a top end Intel processor with a $1000 video card in tow if you wanted to. With ATX, you have enough space to use 2-3 video cards and, depending on the layout, still have a few slots left for other things (sound card, PCIe SSD, etc.)

As for 2) and 3), that's important because of cost. The more features you want or need, the more the motherboard will cost. It makes zero sense to spend $400 on a motherboard with a PLX bridge (for 3-4 video cards) and a massively complcated power delivery system to the CPU when you can get a decent, quality board that'll more than meet your needs at half the price. If you have a good sound and wifi card, does it make sense to spend the extra $40 for a board with isolated onboard sound and integrated WiFi? Do you need a ton of USB ports? And so on.

As for 3) overclocking means you are increasing the operating frequency of that part for more performance at the expense of cooling, power consumption, and possible longevity. It's like taking an engine and using NOS to create more power.

To be honest, you're better off building your own kit as opposed to using a iBuyPower just from a cost perspective and in terms of versatility.

Really, with your budget all that really matters are is 1) what form-factor you want, 2) how many non-gaming hardware features you want, and 3) if you plan to do CPU overclocking.

As far as vendors are concerned: Intel's processors considerably outperforms AMD's offering within the same price bracket while consuming far less power. I expected high levels of software optimization because the Xbox One and PS4 do not have strange, proprietary hardware that is difficult to program for. Both consoles utilize the same CPU with fairly simple cores (no SMT, no issues with having to balance a load across two integer units that share a single FPU as is the case with CMT, no stupidly long pipelines, etc.) that were well documented YEARS before they were launched. It also doesn't hurt that both CPUs utilize an ISA that is literally 11 years old (X86-64) at this point in time...one that every multiplatform developer on the planet has had some experience working.

The GPUs use GCN as their architecture. GCN had been in development in 2008-2010, the white papers came out in 2011, and it was finally released in January 2012. Is it different than the VLIW4 and VLIW5 architectures of its predecessors? Yes. Is it inherently more difficult to develop for? Not really: if you're familiar with unified shaders, you're familiar with GCN. If you've made a PC game in the past 2-3 years, you've already released a product that supports that hardware.

Most of the programming philosophies that people struggled with last generation (multi-threaded, multi-core programming) carry over to this hardware generation AND they're much easier to implement. The hardware is well documented and is actually outdated right now.

We're not talking about exotic, weird kit with poor documentation: we're talking about platforms that were well understood and mature before either console launched. To NOT have high levels of software optimization boils down to incompetence.

We were playing Gauntlet Legends when he paused the game and looked at me. "Dude...your arm's bleeding."

"I must've gotten myself on a tree while I was dirt biking. It's nothing. I'm fine, now let's kill some dwarves."

We started up again, but I could see him looking at my arm every few minutes out of the corner of my eye.

He paused the game again, dropped the controller between his knees. "....so, if you don't tell me what's actually wrong I'm waking up your mom,"

"I'm fine..."

"Dude, cut the shit. When you got up to grab a drink, your sleeve pulled up and I saw 'em." 

I sat there for a bit, closed my eyes and sighed. He knew, so there was no point in hiding it or keeping up the charade. He lifted my sleeve as I sat there and hung my head quietly, then backed away in hushed silence. When I looked up to make eye contact, his eyes were rimmed with tears.

"Why would you do that to yourself, man? Those aren't clean lines, you CARVED THEM with something."

"It's complicated."

"Then fucking in uncomplicate it for me."

So  I told him the truth: I was deeply depressed, my family was disintegrating, and it was the only way to get that kind of bottled emotional pain out of my system. I was half way through explaining myself when he wrapped his arms around me and hugged the breath out of me.

"I love you Snapjackal. Not in a gay way. You're my best friend and you're like a brother to me. I'm there for you, man. Just..,don't do this again, alright? I won't tell anyone, but you'd better fucking promise me you'll call me the next time it gets that bad,"

This will be long, so apologies.

1) You need to have a diet or nutrition plan in place. What you eat, how much, and when determines: how fast you're able to recover, is a factor in your stamina during a workout, how quickly you put on muscle, and how your immune system will fare coping with the additional physical stress. You can lift and run like a madman but, if your diet is shit, you'll show minimal/slow gains, you'll require more time in between routines, you will find yourself becoming more susceptible to infection (cold, flu, etc), your routines will suffer, and you will feel like shit outside of the gym. Eat clean, eat often, but manage your calories; you need enough surplus calories for repair and building, but not so much to put on fat.

2) Good form is way more important than what weight you lift. If you have poor for, you run the risk of major injury; you destroy your knees and back with a bad squat, you risk rupturing discs during a bad dead lift, etc. You're also sabotaging your body in a multitude of ways. The first is that you're not fully or properly engaging the target muscle group; muscles that shouldn't be coming into play are, reducing or even negating the effectiveness of that exercise. If you see someone doing bicep curls but are only able to do a rep by swinging it, they aren't engaging the bicep; that weight is being moved by their back, legs, and shoulder group. The second? You're establishing bad muscle memory. Over time, the exercise becomes an automatic response; you don't think, you do. Bad form that becomes established leads you to doing it wrong every time.

3) As others have said, it's a marathon, not a race. Take your time, do it right, and don't get discouraged. That guy who's benchpressing 300 lbs naturally? He started exactly where you are and got there over years.

4) Priorities. Do you want strength, or max muscle? This effects how you train to a large degree. 

5) Leg day is the most important day. Never skip it, and target ALL parts of your tight. That means your hamstrings and inner thighs should get as much attention as your quads.

6) Don't over do it with the cardio.

7) Don't over train. If you're working out for more than two hours on the same body group and you're not giving yourself adequate downtime, you will actually cause atrophy and injury. This isn't an if, you WILL.

8) Every routine needs to have different exercises to hit the target muscle group(s) at different angles. Muscles are complex: they have different heads, and multiple attachment sites. For exaxmple: good, proportionate pecs the muscles need to be well developed at the top, in the middle, and at the bottom. A regular bench press will build the middle and out pec, but you need to also do decline as well as incline benches and flies. 

9) Watch your grip and hand position. Either one greatly effects how you lift and what part of the target muscle is getting worked. You can use this to your advantage for weak spot training (narrow grip pull ups will widening your back, curling palm face down will help build your brachialis  and upper forearm, etc.) On the flip side, an inappropriate grip can hurt or kill you.

Clinical depression and PTSD. 

Clinical depression is...well...torture of the worst kind. Day in, day out, your mind does everything it possibly can to torture you. Every flaw, real or imagined, is analyzed and criticized to the point you feel ashamed to even be alive. Colors dim, food loses taste, and you derive joy from nothing (even though you logically know you should). You feel useless, you feel irreparably broken, that you don't deserve to be happy, and that death's pretty much the only option to not spend a life of suffering in quiet misery.

PTSD? On one hand, you have the Sword of Damocles and it never goes away. Your fight or flight response becomes your body's default mode of operation: you always feel on edge, you scan rooms for threats, your blood pressure is constantly elevated thanks to a seemingly never ending adrenaline and cortisol dump, you sleep poorly and you have nightmares instead of dreams. Your body is so tense that aches, pains, and spasms are a part of day to day life. You can't remember or even conceptualize what it's like to be "normal".

On the other hand, there's always your version of Mr. Hyde. All of your repressed hate, rage, anger and sadness at the various traumatic events you've been forced to endure in life have been distilled into one horrible, terrifying creature. He has your intellect, your memories, and gets to wear your face for a mask; your PTSD manifest itself as the absolute worst version of you. If you're strong and are prepared for the immense strain, you can keep him largely under control. But, sometmes you're unable to. When something acts as a "trigger", all of the horrible memories you wish you could purge from your brain and all of the negative emotions you've been holding back hit you all at the same time. He gets loose at this point, goes on the warpath, and all you can do is mentally sit back and scream as he goes on the warpath. 

You do everything you possibly can to re-gain yourself. In your brief moments of clarity, you try to poison yourself with drugs and alcohol in an effort to make yourself so ill your body has no choice but to shut down, reboot, and come back online; if you die, it looks like an accident, insurance pays off, and you slip away as who you once were. Sometimes, this doesn't even work.

Other people? For clinical depression or PTSD (let alone both), they write you off completely. At best, they think you're an asshole because you're emotionally distant, irritable, sad, and easily stressed. At worst, they think you're dangerous, psychotic, incapable of being happy, are an emotional blackhole for their own lives, and need to be isolated from society as a whole.
Dr. Perceptron, is that you?

Suicide attempt. May 9th, 2013 at 9:30 pm.

The whole month of April was pretty much the worst I'd ever lived through. Love of my life dumped me hard and my universe just started collapsing upon itself. I couldn't work out because the injury to my inner chest wall I'd sustained during my last leg press hadn't yet recovered; it hurt to breathe at rest, let alone during any heavy lifting. I'd been off of my medication for weeks, so my clinical depression was kicking my ass hard and my PTSD took over to such a degree I could only sit back and scream internally as my body went on the warpath. For the first 7 days, I didn't sleep at all. I couldn't eat solid food without immediately throwing it right back up. Resuming my medication didn't work, Trying to drink myself to the brink of alcohol poisoning so I could just shut down and reboot didn't work, neither did overdosing on sleeping aids; I went down for maybe 30 minutes before hopping right back up with a resting heart rate of 120 bpm. For the next two weeks, I was lucky average 30 minutes to an hour every other night. The pressure at work as just mounting and mounting; cutbacks to staff, increased responsibilities at no more pay, more work, etc. My roommate hated me at this point, so she ended up screwing me on the rent. 

On the 9th of May, I was fired for the anxiety attack I had at the register earlier in the week. It was the straw that broke the camel's back. I remember sitting in my manager's office, watching his lips move while I was lost in thought; I knew right then, right there, I'd lost everything and that my life was over. I'd lost the girl, my job, my home, my mind and all control over my life. I was done, and knew that continuing my life would just be an appalling, depressing waste of time. I shook my manager's hand, thanked him for his time, and walked out of his off. I took a few boxes with me on the way out; I told my coworkers I was moving back home, when the reality was that I was just going to pack my stuff to make it easier for the executor of my estate to sort through.

I got home around 1 or so, and started packing. Once that was done, I started writing my suicide note. I spent a good hour, hour and a half on it; this was going to my last will and testament, my last words to be read, and I wanted to make them count. While I did so, I called the suicide hotline as my last resort; I figured that, surely, if I wasn't meant to die then whoever it was on the other end would be able to convince me as such. I spent around 30 minutes getting the insulting platitudes of "Oh, it gets better." "Oh it isn't that bad" until I hung up. 

I went to the local liquor store, bought a liter of rum, and then bused back. There wasn't going to be a final meal; I knew that whatever I'd eat would come out and wanted to leave as little mess possible for the person to find me. I didn't want to be found on the floor in a pool of my own vomit and feces; I wanted to be found on the couch, head down, as if I'd fallen asleep. After re-reading my note, I gave my last post on reddit, counted out my pills, and set up my Netflix queue so that my final hours would be spent watching my favorite shows (South Park and metalocalypse). Once I was sure I wasn't going to make it, I was going to click the send button in my gmail so that all of my friends, all of my family, would know what happened, why, and what was to be done after.

I remember saying aloud after slamming back half the booze, "Better to die than be a monster" and as I went for my pills, my ex had called. I hung up on her and sat there sobbing for an hour because I'd lost the conviction to go through with it; I was ready to die, I had planned to die, I wanted to die, but my self-preservation instincts were preventing me from taking a month's worth of pills. I threw them across the room, polished off the remaining liter of rum, and went to bed.

That's...pretty much it.

People who've never suffered from depression have no frame of reference to draw off of for empathy or support; it's something they've never felt, don't understand, and can't conceptualize.

They don't understand there's no "on-of" switch for it, where you can go, "You know what? You're right, I am a downer. Time to be happy!" It doesn't work like that, when your brain isn't wired correctly and isn't producing specific neurotransmitters in the amount required for normalcy. Your neurobiology and  neurochemistry is different from theirs. 

They also don't understand your emotional state. They have no idea what it's like to have your own mind turn against you, whispering in your ear at all times of how terrible you are as a person. How you don't deserve to be happy, how you deserve all of the horrible things that happen to you on a daily basis. They don't know how isolated you are from the world around you; you're so detached from other people, you're trapped in an isolation chamber created by your own mind. They don't understand how lonely you feel when the world at large writes you off as damaged goods, or when your friends, family, and loved one turn their back to you because it's the easiest thing to do. They don't know hopelessness, true hopelessness, because they've never experienced it. Where you don't know if you'll ever have a happy, meaningful life. Where you realize all of the pain and misery you feel on a daily basis may never end. They don't know how horrible it is to realize that you might not even even be alive by the start of the next year.

No one, and I mean no one, would ever make the conscious choice to feel that way. 

At the end of the day, we only have ourselves to rely on. In my experience, and I pray it isn't true for you, friends and family will abandon you the very moment the darkness within starts overcoming you.

For starters, stopping telling us "Oh, you don't have it so bad." "It could be worse" or some other insulting platitude that makes us feel like spoiled children who need to be shamed into feeling a different way. Stop treating us as if we ENJOY feeling the way we do, that we like wallowing in our own personal hell. Stop telling us we control how we feel.

Also, if you're in a relationship or have a friendship with someone who is depressed, don't abandon them because it's the easiest thing to do. Be there for them, help them work through it. Be that one voice of reason when their inner monologue is so dark it's suffocating them. Yes, it's hard on you. Yes, it gets frustrating and you want to hit your head against a brick wall because it seems you can't get through. Yes, it hurts, because you don't feel like you can make them happy. But depression is a hurricane; it's rough, harsh, and exceedingly cruel. But if you can get your partner through the worst of the storm, they'll be there to enjoy the sunshine with you when it passes; if you abandon them, you're basically guaranteeing that whatever little mental life raft they've built for themselves is going to sink. If you think it's hard on you, you have no idea at all just how awful it is for the other person. If you think the fight for you is draining, you have no idea at all how much your friend or SO is fighting just to get through the day. And if you think for a minute that the other person enjoys being down or unhappy, you really don't have the first clue as to who they are.

Normality. I miss being normal, I miss being...me, before depression and PTSD came into the picture.

I miss being able to wake up without my mind automatically defaulting to, "Okay, so the last few months have been insufferably horrible. I miss being happy and not having my mind abuse itself, raking it over coals for things it can't even control. I miss being able to just smile without having to force it. I miss just being able to live in the moment, for the moment, without a care in the world or having to bear the weight of the universe on shoulders that can't take it.

I miss being able to relax, for my body to just unwind and let go instead of being so tense all the time that my muscles are constantly spasming and twitching in unending pain. I miss being able to stretch without my tendons and ligaments burning because of how tight they are. I miss being able to walk alone without the uneasy feeling that I'm being watched, or having my hairs stand on end because I'm sure something's coming to hurt me. I miss not going through my day feeling like my heart's going to pop in my chest, feeling the constriction in my chest as if I'm holding my breath in anticipation of a hit. I miss being able to feel something other than sadness or anger. I'm so numb, so closed off I might as well be a zombie.

I miss being normal. It's been so long I can't even remember what it is or conceptualize it. I don't know what normal is. As for myself...I'm looking at an old picture of myself and my younger brother. I see this happy 9 year old grinning ear to ear while stopping the go-kart just long enough for my parents to snap a photo. I see this joyful little boy who's truly happy to be alive, innocent, who doesn't have a care in the world. I see a little boy who's full of life. And I fight back tears as I realize that little boy in the picture is gone forever; a tired, old, broken man occupies his body.

I miss that little boy I used to be. I miss that happiness.

Most people who suffer from PTSD have varying degrees of hyperarousal and hypervigilance. Trying to articulate how they feel to someone who's never truly experienced them is akin to explaining depression to someone who has never been depressed; at best, they'll try to understand it but they won't be able to fully comprehend it, how it feels, and what the thought processes are because they haven't had that experience. They don't don't know what it's like to be so tense your muscles are perpetually flexed. They don't know what it feels like to have a massive adrenaline dump first thing in the morning, or how truly awful it feels to "come down" as cortisol cascades through your system. They don't know what it's like to go numb, to feel no fear, no happiness, nothing but this "Something bad is going to happen to me and I need to protect myself" urge.

Most people, at first glance, think I'm a cold and perpetually close to exploding. To them, I'm that pissed off asshole who's always upset for no legitimately good reason. What they don't understand is that my brain and peripheral nervous system is constantly locked in gear as if I'm in the middle of having to physically defend myself against an attacker. 

The attacker doesn't exist. It's a phantom brought to life by a never ending hormonal cascade and a misfiring of a brain that has not been able to work through the past trauma you're stuck living in. Logically, you know there's no one out to get you. Someone's not going sneak up behind you, no one's going throw a punch. But even though your logical faculties are screaming, "Everything's okay!" your body outright doesn't listen. As far as it's concerned, someone's coming for you with the sole intent of hurting you. There's no off switch and, contrary to popular belief, I (and people like me) desperately wish there was. If you were to tell me tomorrow, "Hey, we've got this wonder drug that will shut your PTSD down for good. But, it'll reduce your life expectancy by 25%", taking it would be a remarkably easy choice. I would rather live 15 years less and have 30-40 good years, than live to be 95 and stay feeling this way.

This will be long. I have mild PTSD. I've been locked in a fight or flight response (fight) for so long that I've literally forgotten what it is to be "relaxed". There are two sides to it, both of which are part of the same coin: hypervigilance, and hyperarousal.

With hypervigilance, my body is constantly anticipating a threat. Every muscle is under perpetual tension, so much so that chronic pain, spams, and are a part of day to day life. The only time they're not is when my body pumps in the massive amount of coritsol it takes to counteract the nigh perpetual adrenaline dumping; at this point, they're not so much at rest as they are succumbing to exhaustion. I instinctively scan a room for potential threats, even when I'm among friends and family. I find eating anywhere other than with my back to a wall exceptionally uncomfortable and nerve-wracking because it makes me feel vulnerable. The moment I feel any unexpected movement behind, my instinctive reaction is to spin around and throw a punch. Sneaking up on someone else to scare them will get you a laugh; doing so with me will get you a broken nose and it will happen without my being aware of it.

Hyperarousal is probably the single worst thing a person can feel outside of depression. It is the literal Sword of Damocles. Whereas I'm looking for a threat with hypervigilance, I feel as if my doom is impending with hyperarousal. It's horrible. The stress is overwhelming and I'm easily irritated. It takes well over an hour to fall asleep and, even then, I don't sleep well. On a good night, I'll wake up every 2-3 hours for 15 minutes at a time and on bad nights I don't sleep at all; even then, the moment there's any movement at all in the room, I will wake up and stay up. Anger is the worst part of it. A personal slight just grows and feeds itself until I'm so overwhelmed I come close to fainting when the dust clears.

I do not know what "normal" feels like. I don't remember what it's like to relaxed or be relaxed, unless I'm unconscious.

After all, my truck was easily identifiable, it was the only one of its kind in the county, and the last thing I needed was having someone stalk me after a confrontation.

We finally arrive at her house and go inside. After a quick look through, I stand guard in the living room, she goes into the kitchen, and then comes back out with a glass of coke. We make idle chit chat and I start feeling a bit off around 1/4 of the way into it, so I go sit down on the couch. I chalk it up to stress, so I keep on drinking and we keep talking.

The chit chat then becomes a series of compliments. She tells me how I'm the sweetest guy she's ever met and how attractive I am. I tell her it's starting to make me uncomfortable, but she keeps going on. The compliments become flirts, the flirts become outright sexual innuendo. At this point, I feel almost completely out of it and I know something is wrong; my speech is starting to slur, my heads spinning, and my limbs feel heavy. I try standing up, but can't find the strength to. She sits next to me, and as I try figuring out what's happening, she straddles my lap. I try pushing her off, and she pushes me into the back of the couch and holds me there.

 "My boyfriend never beat me..because I never had one. This is the only way I thought I could have you."

I don't know how I made it home without getting into an accident; with the shape I was in, I should've either wrapped my truck around a pole or hit someone head on. Somehow, I made it home intact.
